limitations: Single real ZkTestServer and one client; the schedule is the previously evidenced one, reproduced with the archived diagnostic's seams (log-appender callback hold and creation gating). Ordering observations rest on that hold: B Expired was delivered while event dispatch was occupied by the held callback, as in the prior runs.

The liveness control's during-disconnect snapshot was taken after the replacement had already reconnected through the half-closed proxy; disconnect application itself was verified by a bounded wait for the manager to report disconnected before the snapshot, and keeper-creation and session assertions bracket the whole window.
No Docker-dependent proof was run or credited; existing PR CI for this head was not repeated, per the gate.

archived_diagnostic_at_new_head.failure: AssertionError at ConnectionManagerRealZkRecoveryTest.java:137, assertTrue(manager.isConnectedAndNotClosed()), immediately after the recovery latch fired: the manager reported not-connected although the replacement session was installed and its keeper connected. The stale-callback rejection and recovery assertions before it passed.

liveness_control.detail: Replacement B expired never issued; B disconnected via proxy half-close, disconnect applied (bounded wait for manager disconnected passed), no new keeper created during the window (creations stayed 2), installed session remained B (0x100000fe18d0003) and the installed keeper was still B, and B reconnected with the same session; manager reconnected. A replacement that is alive but temporarily disconnected is retained and is not replaced.

schedule.control_client: An independently connected control client reached the real server while B was expired, so server reachability during the schedule is proven.
schedule.sequence: A (0x100000fb6000002) expired, expired-path entry 1; B (0x100000fb6000003) created, its SyncConnected held in the log appender before state application; B Disconnected delivered and applied (manager disconnected); B expired on the server; B Expired delivered at trace t=5652ms while dispatch was still occupied by the held callback; B terminal confirmed.

stale_expiry_question.c_installed_before_b_expired_processed: Yes. The A-expiry reconnect loop, whose update was waiting on keeper B, hit the new keeper-liveness check after B died, retried, and requested keeper C (attempt 3) at t=6671ms, before the held callback was released. The held stale B SyncConnected was released at t=6672ms and rejected as stale at t=6673ms. C was created at t=6674ms, connected at t=6677ms, installed, and onReconnect fired (count 1) at t=6678ms. B's queued Expired was processed only at t=6679ms (expired-path entry 2); the entry count was still 1 at release time.
stale_expiry_question.effect_of_processing_queued_b_expired: The unconditional expired() applied on top of the healthy installed C: it ran a second reconnect cycle that created keeper D (attempt 4, created t=6681ms, connected t=6684ms), closed the healthy C keeper (Closed event t=6789ms), and invoked onReconnect a second time (count 2, t=6789ms). After a 5-second settle window the installed session was D's, not C's (4 keeper creations total); the manager then read connected and not likely-expired. Between C's install and D's connect the manager's connected flag was down, which is the state the archived diagnostic's final assertion caught.

summary: Controlled real-ZooKeeper diagnostic completed at Houston's exact head 684354d21476e44458e45c83a810dd25d16ba284 (tree c2660c8702d19bd9548ca98b23cd22f82d6fd02c). The previously evidenced schedule was fully reproduced with real sessions. Observed: the replacement C connected and was installed before the queued B Expired was processed, and processing that stale expiry then started a further keeper D, closed the healthy C, and fired the reconnect callbacks a second time; recovery is eventual (via D) but the healthy session is not left in place. The archived recovery diagnostic fails at this head on exactly that transient: its final isConnectedAndNotClosed assertion, taken right after the first recovery, is false. The disconnected-but-alive replacement control was retained with its session intact, and the existing nightly reconnect stress test passes. No source, test, branch, or PR changes were made.
